paper.title: Comparison of techniques for handling missing covariate data within prognostic modelling studies: a simulation study
paper.citation: Marshall A, Altman DG, Royston P, Holder RL. Comparison of techniques for handling missing covariate data within prognostic modelling studies: a simulation study. BMC Medical Research Methodology 10:7 (2010)

inputs.name: TH.data 1.1-2 (GBSG2, the motivating data; Ubuntu 24.04 r-cran-th.data)

items.label: Table 1, means and SDs after transformation
Skewness of X2, X3, X4, X8 (Methods text)

assumptions.what: Skewness b1 = m3 / s^3 with the n - 1 SD, on the raw scale (the paper does not define it)
assumptions.sensitivity: g1 and G1 give 2.88 / 4.78 / 3.08 / 1.77 and 2.88 / 4.79 / 3.09 / 1.78: three of four fields miss by 0.01

items.label: Correlations quoted in the Methods text

assumptions.what: Pearson correlations on the raw (untransformed) scale
assumptions.sensitivity: On the transformed scale X3-X4 is 0.64 and X2-X8 0.29: two of four fields miss

items.label: Fig. 1, histograms of the covariates (a) and the transformed covariates (b)

assumptions.what: Published values are read from the article PDF's vector figures: each plotted point is a vertex of the series' line, each axis is mapped from its tick marks and printed labels; the PDF writer's coordinate grid is 0.405 pt
assumptions.sensitivity: One grid step is added to every tolerance; the tick fits have residuals below 0.3% of a tick interval

items.label: Linear predictor, full Cox model on the breast cancer data (Methods equation)

assumptions.what: Efron ties (R's default); X8 as two dummies at 20 and 30 mm
assumptions.sensitivity: Breslow ties give X3 -0.00228, still -0.0023 printed: same 9 of 9

items.label: About 35% censored (Methods text)

assumptions.what: Binary covariates X5 to X7 are the multivariate normal draw cut at 0.5, as the text says; this weakens their correlation with the other covariates (X1 with X6: 0.77 in the data, 0.61 generated)
assumptions.sensitivity: Keeping the observed correlations moves the empirical SE of X1 from 0.0051 to 0.0064 and of X6 from 0.104 to 0.132 (paper 0.0060 and 0.119); see truth_variants.json

assumptions.what: Hazards are per day, 2-year survival at 730.5 days, predicted at the means of all covariates
assumptions.sensitivity: The full-data 2-year survival is 0.776 against the figure's 0.78

cause.summary: The text's 'approximately 35%' is a rounded figure: the stated hazards (0.0002 for censoring against 0.00027 exp(LP) for events) give 36.4% censored in our run and 36.6% with every variant of our generator.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Our binary covariates or the floor at 0 change the censoring
hypotheses.test: Censored share of 20,000 cohorts under each generator variant (truth_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The stated hazards give about 36%, which the text rounds to 35
hypotheses.test: Every variant gives 36.6% (2000 cohorts each) and our 200 replicates 36.4%

items.label: Missingness design: incomplete cases, shares and overlaps (Methods text)

assumptions.what: Missingness intercepts solved at the average value of each mechanism's term; continuous terms (and survival time, as log(t / SD(t))) divided by their SD
assumptions.sensitivity: Realised shares in text.design

cause.summary: Each covariate is missing in exactly its share of all cases (X3 at 25%: 67.98% of 25.75% incomplete cases is 17.50% of all cases, the design's 0.70 x 25%), but the overall share of incomplete cases runs 0.3 to 0.8 points above the target because only three pairs of indicators are tied (X5 and X3 or X8 and X2 can be missing together by chance). The shares of incomplete cases then fall slightly below the stated ones. The paper's numbers are design targets ('approximately'), and how it tied the other pairs is not stated.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The per-covariate rates are wrong
hypotheses.test: Share of incomplete cases times the incomplete rate against the design's share times the level, every level (comparison.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Untied pairs of indicators add incomplete cases
hypotheses.test: The excess of incomplete cases over the target (0.3 to 0.8 points) against the chance overlap of X5 with X3 and of X8 with X2 under independence

items.label: Table 2, specification of the missingness mechanisms

cause.summary: A design input, used as given (the blank X3 cell of the combined mechanism read as MCAR).

items.label: Table 3, odds ratios between missingness indicators

assumptions.what: The shares become whole cases of 1000, rounded half up, before the odds ratio is taken
assumptions.sensitivity: With unrounded shares 8 of 15 odds ratios match (10% and 50% columns and X2|MX3 at 75%); rounding half to even gives 45.14 -> 19.42 at 5% for X8|MX3

items.label: Table 4, the missing data methods

cause.summary: A list of methods and settings, implemented as given in the package.

items.label: Figs 2 and 3, reference lines: true values and empirical SEs (20,000 complete-data cohorts)

assumptions.what: Published values are read from the article PDF's vector figures: each plotted point is a vertex of the series' line, each axis is mapped from its tick marks and printed labels; the PDF writer's coordinate grid is 0.405 pt
assumptions.sensitivity: One grid step is added to every tolerance; the tick fits have residuals below 0.3% of a tick interval

assumptions.what: Binary covariates X5 to X7 are the multivariate normal draw cut at 0.5, as the text says; this weakens their correlation with the other covariates (X1 with X6: 0.77 in the data, 0.61 generated)
assumptions.sensitivity: Keeping the observed correlations moves the empirical SE of X1 from 0.0051 to 0.0064 and of X6 from 0.104 to 0.132 (paper 0.0060 and 0.119); see truth_variants.json

assumptions.what: Back-transformed X3 and X4 below 0 set to 0 (the text gives upper limits only)
assumptions.sensitivity: Without the floor the true values move by less than their Monte Carlo error (truth_variants.json)

cause.summary: Our generator's empirical SEs are 14% smaller for X1 and X6 and 14% larger for X4 than the paper's, and its true values 1 to 5% larger in magnitude for X2, X3, X4 and X5 (X7 0.8%). Keeping the binaries' observed correlations takes the X1 and X6 SEs past the paper's (0.0064 and 0.132 against 0.0060 and 0.119, ours 0.0051 and 0.104); the unrounded coefficients move X2's true value from 0.0517 to 0.0513 (paper 0.0507); the X4 SE and the larger magnitudes stay open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The binary covariates of the paper kept their observed correlations (the 0.5 cut-point weakens X1 with X6 from 0.77 to 0.61)
hypotheses.test: True-value cohorts with the binaries' covariances divided by the attenuation of the cut (truth_variants.json, 2000 cohorts)

hypotheses.hypothesis: The paper generated survival from the unrounded Cox coefficients (its true values equal them to three figures)
hypotheses.test: True-value cohorts with GBSG2's unrounded coefficients (truth_variants.json)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Setting back-transformed X3 and X4 below 0 to 0 moves the true values
hypotheses.test: True-value cohorts without the floor (truth_variants.json)

cause.summary: Most points fall within Monte Carlo error. Most of the 32 misses are estimates of X2, X3, X4 and X5 at 50 and 75% (five at 25%), mostly MI and SI, where our MIX without truncating, MICE-PMM and SI are further from or nearer the truth than the paper's. The offset of the true values does not explain them; the 2004 to 2005 package versions could not be tested.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The offset between our true values and the paper's explains the misses
hypotheses.test: Compare each point's bias from its own run's true value instead of its value (comparison.json, bias_relative_to_own_truth)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Monte Carlo error at 200 replicates
hypotheses.test: Tolerance of three combined Monte Carlo SEs; at that tolerance chance alone misses about 1 point in 370, and the misses cluster in a few covariates and methods instead of spreading

hypotheses.hypothesis: The imputation packages changed since 2004 to 2005 (mice 1.13.1, Hmisc 2.2-3, norm 1.0-9, mix 1.0-4 against mice 3.16.0, Hmisc 5.1-1, norm 1.0-11.1, mix 1.0-13), and with them the defaults the paper does not state
hypotheses.test: Not run: mice 1.13.1 is not in the CRAN archive and the 2004 packages do not build on R 4.3

page.lede: {items} results: {exact} exact, {agrees} agree, {partly} partly agree, {differs} differ, {not_attempted} not attempted. The lost simulation was rebuilt from the paper as an R package and run again, and every plotted point was read back out of the paper's own figures.
page.items_caption: Every figure, table and claim of the paper. A figure point agrees when it is within 3 combined Monte Carlo standard errors and one PDF grid step of the published one; long lists show only the points that miss.
page.claims_line: The main claim holds: MICE-PMM without transformation is the least biased MI method for the skewed covariates, stays within 10% bias at 25% (MAR), and is more than 0.5 SE from the truth at 50% under MAR, MCAR and the combined mechanism, and every MI method is more than 0.5 SE off for X3 under MNAR from 25%. The text contradicts its own figures in 18 claim fields; the 12 where our run agrees with the figures are counted as paper errors. The claims that differ follow the generated covariates and the newer imputation packages (open).
came_back: Every mean and SD from the breast cancer data.
The skewness, the correlations and the Cox model of the Methods, to the printed digit.
Every bar tall enough to read (82).
All 15 odds ratios, once the shares are counted as whole cases.
Most plotted points within Monte Carlo error, read from the paper's vector figures.
The simulation and the nine missing data methods, as the R package misscox.
buried: The simulation code, its seeds and its 1000 data sets were never released.
How the paper's binary covariates kept their correlations: ours lose some, and the SEs of age and menopausal status come out about 14% smaller.
How the paper pooled the likelihood ratio test after imputation: no rule we tried gives its p-values.
The 2004 to 2005 imputation packages: mice 1.13.1 is gone, the others do not build on today's R.
page.matched_intro: How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.
matched: GBSG2 from the CRAN package TH.data: 686 patients, the eight covariates of Table 1.
Multivariate normal on the transformed scale, back-transformed, cut and truncated; exponential event and censoring times.
Logistic models per covariate with Table 3's odds ratios, four mechanisms, five levels.
CC, SI and seven MI methods with norm, mix, mice and Hmisc, 20 imputations.
The full Cox model, Rubin's rules, Li's pooled test, R2, D and 2-year survival.
page.closing: Missing covariates in Cox models came back from the paper's text, its data and its own vector figures.
